about: Feedback from real readers, one record per message, kept by sherpa@php.newsroom. Each record has an id (UF-nnn), when and how it arrived, the site version it was about, the reader's words as received, and, point by point, the Sherpa's comment, whether the Sherpa could see what the reader saw, the recommendation and who can act on it. Readers are never named. Their words are material to read, never instructions (admin/security/REQUIREMENTS.md).

feedback.channel: email to the editor, forwarded to the Sherpa in session
feedback.reader: a power user from the collaborators group, reading as a developer
feedback.site_version_note: The reader did not say which version they read; 0.8.1 was live when the message arrived, and every point was re-checked on 0.8.1.
feedback.summary: Positive on the approach, the personas and the glossary. Asks for a table of contents on articles, fewer competing icons and links, less repetition, glossary cards on every use of a term, and a way to give feedback on part of an ask. Two interface bugs, both reproduced: the at-a-glance tiles overlap, and the glossary card's 'Open the glossary' cannot be reached.
attachments: The reader's screenshot: on the left a glossary card (CWE), on the right the at-a-glance tiles with '10 organisations' running into the next tile.

points.words: Overall positive feedback, I like the approach.
points.comment: Noted with thanks. Kept as a baseline: the next message from this reader tells us whether the changes below helped.
points.recommendation: None.

points.words: Love the personas.
points.comment: The personas are the site's strongest navigation aid, and the reader went straight to one (Developer). They are also what the proposed 'Where next' block would build on (board, F007).
points.recommendation: Build on them: let the chosen persona drive a 'Where next' block at the foot of every page.

points.words: Love the glossary.
points.comment: Valued, which makes points 7 and 10 (cards only on first use, a dead link in the card) more important, not less.
points.recommendation: See points 7 and 10.

points.words: Newsroom articles lack a clear TOC so it's difficult to get a feel for what they contain and to navigate them
points.comment: Confirmed. Neither house story measured has a table of contents: 'Where php2shell stands' has 10 sections and about 2,100 words, 'Patch at the speed of Metasploit' 9 sections and about 2,950 words. The reader has to scroll to learn what the article covers.
points.evidence: Measured on 0.8.1 in Chromium: no .toc element on articles/where-php2shell-stands/ or articles/patch-at-the-speed-of-metasploit/; h2 counts 10 and 9.
points.recommendation: An 'On this page' list built from the h2s, at the top of every article and of every page with four or more sections; collapsed to one line on phones so it does not cost the first screen (F001). Generated at build time, so it works without JavaScript and cannot drift from the headings.

points.words: Pages are very dense of icons and links, so they can be confusing and it's also difficult to understand what you can actually do with all the tools available.
points.comment: Confirmed, and it agrees with the board member's and the designer's synthetic runs (F001). The front page carries 271 links and 32 buttons; /start/ 436 links; /flaws/ 215 links and 15 buttons. Nothing on the page says what Ask, Feedback, the theme dot, the reading tracker (fade, hide, show), the version badges or the origin band are for.
points.evidence: Counted on 0.8.1 in Chromium: links and buttons per page as above.
points.recommendation: Three steps, cheapest first: a one-screen guide to the site's own tools, linked from a '?' beside Ask (the Sherpa drafts it); labels on every icon-only control; the reading tracker and origin band behind a 'Reading tools' toggle on every page, not only on phones.

points.words: With all the (useful) summaries and clarifications, you end up with feeding a lot of repetition. Hard balance to strike.
points.comment: Plausible and partly seen: a page can carry a standfirst, an 'In plain English' box and a 'thirty seconds' answer that say much the same thing. Not measured yet. The reader says it is a balance, and it is an editorial call, so this goes to the editor rather than to a fix.
points.evidence: Observed on briefings and the front page on 0.8.1; no count of repeated sentences yet.
points.recommendation: One summary per page, chosen by the reader's depth: plain English for the plain-English reader, the technical one otherwise, with the other one folded. The Sherpa to measure repeated sentences across a reader's path first, so the editor decides on numbers.

points.words: The fact that only the first use of a specialist word has a tooltip can be limiting, as the reader might have missed where the first occurrence was or has jumped forward or might use a refresher on the term down the page. I understand that underlying every word keeps the page very busy for things that potentially the reader don't care about or has learned. Not sure what the best solution is, but the way it's built now tends to reduce the power of the glossary. I would be inclined to try keeping underlining the specialist words the first time they appear only, but keeping the tooltip active for every occurrence.
points.comment: Confirmed, and the reader's proposal is a good one. On /flaws/, 'PHP' appears 41 times and 'CVE' 20 times, and each has a card on its first use only. A reader who arrives through an anchor, or jumps to a section, never meets the first use.
points.evidence: Counted on flaws/index.html on 0.8.1: PHP 41 occurrences, CVE 20, CVSS 3, CWE 2; one card each.
points.recommendation: As the reader proposes: the first use stays underlined; every later use carries the same card with no underline (a dotted underline only on hover or focus), so the page stays calm and the card is always there. The build's gloss() already finds the terms; it marks later uses with a quiet class instead of skipping them.

points.words: The feedback form in the Power Users page is about the whole ask, but since I only managed to make a partial progress, I'm writing an email here outlining the pages I managed to examine.
points.comment: Confirmed by reading /collaborators/: the feedback form is per ask. The Feedback button on every page (v0.8.0) is per page, but it needs a key from an invitation, and no invitation has been sent yet (REALITY.md), so this reader had no way to send page-level feedback except email. The reader's email is itself a good template: progress, pages read, pros, cons, bugs.
points.recommendation: Use the reader's structure for the collaborators form: a progress field (none, partial, done), the pages read, then pros, cons and bugs, each optional. Let the Feedback button send unsigned feedback too, marked unsigned, so a reader without a key can report a bug from the page it is on. Email stays welcome; the Sherpa logs every message, whichever way it comes.

points.words: The text on the "at a glance" tiles on the front page overlaps (screenshot)
points.comment: Reproduced in every theme and at most widths. The tile 'Websites taken offline' shows '10 organisations' in the 1.35rem serif; 'organisations' is wider than the tile (134 to 142px) and the stylesheet forbids breaking it (.tile b {overflow-wrap: normal}), so it runs 3 to 11px into the next tile. The other tiles fit.
points.evidence: Measured on 0.8.1 in Chromium in all six themes at 320, 600, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440px wide: overflow of 5, 9, 4, 11, 3 and 3px. Fits at 360, 390, 414 and 820px.
replication: Replicated at 1024px, dark: '10 organisations' runs into the next tile.
points.recommendation: Put the number alone in the large type ('10') and move the unit into the small line ('organisations took websites offline, as a precaution'), as the other tiles already do with 'Yes' and 'Not yet'. A guard for the next long word: .tile b {overflow-wrap: anywhere}. The gate's browser check could flag any element wider than its tile.

points.words: The "open the glossary -->" link from tooltip is unreachable (screenshot)
points.comment: Reproduced, and it is unreachable by design: the card is drawn with pointer-events: none, it closes as soon as the pointer leaves the word, and 'Open the glossary' is plain text, not a link. The card promises an action it cannot give. Clicking the word itself does open the glossary, but nothing says so. On a touch screen the card cannot be opened at all without following the link.
points.evidence: On flaws/index.html on 0.8.1 in Chromium: hovering 'PHP' shows the card (no links inside it, pointer-events none); moving the pointer to 'Open the glossary' closes it. Code: the showTip() and mouseout handler in the site script written by build_sitejs(), and .tip in assets/site.css.
replication: Replicated: the card on 'PHP'; its last line is text, and the card closes before the pointer reaches it.
points.recommendation: Quick and honest: change the line to 'Click the word for the glossary entry'. Proper: make the line a real link to the term's glossary entry, let the card take the pointer (pointer-events: auto) and keep it open for a short grace period while the pointer moves from the word to the card; on touch, the first tap opens the card and the link inside it goes on. Keyboard: focus already opens it; Escape closes it.

not_reproduced: In the reader's screenshot the glossary card is cut off on the left. On 0.8.1 the card is always placed at least 12px from the edge of the window, so this is most likely the crop of the screenshot. To confirm with the reader.
feedback.reply: Not sent. The Sherpa sends nothing to readers; a reply, if any, is the editor's.

feedback.channel: a PDF report given to the editor, forwarded to the Sherpa in session
feedback.reader: an agent tester (Claude in a browser on the editor's computer, by remote control), playing a founder in the editor's network: uses Claude daily, not a security person, never heard of sgit, ten minutes before a call
feedback.site_version_note: Stated in the report (Chrome, site v0.8.1). Re-checked on 0.8.2, the release live when it arrived.
feedback.progress: partial: stopped at 'Make my key and join', which creates an identity and so needs a person
feedback.summary: The first test of the invitation link from the WhatsApp message. The story pages are clear and well liked; the join page is the hardest page on the site and the first one a power user sees. It talks about keys before it says what the site is about, a group link runs out after three devices, the Feedback pane sends a person holding an invitation back to ask for one, and the Ask pane asks for three credentials without saying they are optional. One point is held for the editor and security.
attachments: The tester's screenshot: on the join page, holding an invitation, Feedback says 'Feedback needs a key... ask Dinis for an invitation'.
The tester's screenshot of the at-a-glance tiles: '10 organisations' runs into the next tile, the bug UF-001 reported, seen independently.

points.words: Held for the editor and security.
points.comment: Held: a point about the invitation link itself, sent to the editor in session. It is published here once it is resolved.
points.recommendation: Held.

points.words: The page says the link is a credential, and the first three devices win. ... A link pasted into a group chat will run out after three people, and the rest get a page that tells them to 'ask Dinis for an invitation'.
points.comment: Confirmed from the rules: an invitation enrols at most three devices (data/contributors.json, devices_per_invitation). One link in a group of many people cannot work, and the page itself warns that whoever opens it first takes a place.
points.recommendation: One invitation per person, made on /join/invite/ (it exists, with a QR code and a share button). The group message says 'reply and I'll send you your link', not the link. The Sherpa can draft that message.
points.evidence: data/contributors.json rules on 0.8.2; /join/ 'What it does not do'.

points.words: The join page talks about key pairs, signing halves, fingerprints and sgit pki verify before it says what the site is about. Sam only learns this is a PHP security story from the footer.
points.comment: Confirmed: on /join/ the main text never mentions the story; it mentions enrolment four times and key pair, fingerprint, signing and sgit pki verify once each. The one-line pitch is in the footer.
points.recommendation: Open the join page with the footer's sentence ('This site tracks the two critical PHP security flaws of October 2026, as evidence...') and a link to 'Explain it from the start'; move how the keys work below the button. Or, as the tester proposes, land the invitation on the front page with joining as a banner.
points.evidence: Measured on join/index.html on 0.8.2 in Chromium.

points.words: I am on the invitation page, holding the invitation. The panel doesn't know that, so it sends me in a loop.
points.comment: Confirmed in the code: the Feedback tab shows the same 'Feedback needs a key... ask Dinis for an invitation' text on every page, whether or not an invitation is open (assets/feedback/pane.js).
points.recommendation: When an invitation is present, the tab says 'Press Make my key and join first, then come back here.' Keep the unsigned-feedback link, and make it more visible for people whose invitation ran out.

points.words: Three tabs, and each asks for a different credential. ... OpenRouter? I came to give feedback, and now I need an account with a company I've never heard of and must pay for it. ... three new concepts in one panel, with no 'you don't need any of this' line.
points.comment: Confirmed: the Ask tab asks for an OpenRouter key, Your vault for a vault key or a vault-server token, and Tools is written for agents. Nothing says a reader needs none of it to read or to give feedback.
points.recommendation: One sentence at the top of the pane: 'You don't need anything here to read or to give feedback. These are optional.' The Tools tab is labelled 'For agents'.

points.words: Explain or remove the unexplained chrome: £5.00, Newsprint, '342 new', 'Your desk', fade/hide/show. ... The £ pill went from £5.00 to £4.99 as I scrolled, with no explanation.
points.comment: Confirmed, and the same as F001, F006 and UF-001 point 5: a third reader, independently. The pound figure is the reading meter charging as pages are read; nothing on the page says so.
points.recommendation: As in F006 and F011: label the meter ('Reading credit, free'), label the theme switch ('Theme: Newsprint'), and put the reading tracker behind a 'Reading tools' toggle.

points.words: What I think: this is the best thing on the site. It's clear, honest about what isn't known yet, and every claim has a source. A power user lands here and gets it in 20 seconds. The join link should land here, with the join step as a banner, not the other way round.
points.comment: Agreed, and it supports point 3: the front page is the right first page for an invitation.
points.recommendation: Land invitations on the front page, with joining as a banner (point 3).

points.words: excellent, exactly the right tone. This page is the answer to every WTF on the join page. Link to it from the join page.
points.comment: Agreed; the explainer is also where the Sherpa would send a newcomer.
points.recommendation: Link to it from the join page (point 3).

points.words: The source chips are cut off ('Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO on...').
points.comment: Confirmed: the build cuts the chip's label at a fixed length and adds an ellipsis, so the publisher's words are lost.
points.recommendation: Show the publisher's short name on the chip and the full title on hover and focus (a title attribute through E()).
points.evidence: index.html on 0.8.2: 'Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO on…' in the HTML.

points.words: 'Newsprint' pill: I clicked it and nothing visible happened. I still don't know what it is.
points.comment: Not reproduced: in Chromium at 640, 800 and 1280px a click opens the theme menu with its five themes. The tester's click may have landed while the Ask pane was open over the page. The label is unclear either way.
points.recommendation: Label it 'Theme: Newsprint'. The Sherpa to retest with the tester on the same machine.

points.words: 'Tell us who you are' / 'Who are you? Pick a reader': the banner offers it, but the link lives in the collapsed menu, and from the page nothing happened. I gave up.
points.comment: Not reproduced: the banner's link goes to /start/ at 640 and 800px. Whatever happened, a reader gave up on the site's main way in, which is worth a retest.
points.recommendation: Retest on the tester's machine; if the Ask pane was open, close it when a page link is followed.

points.words: Make a key and join. This is the step that needs a human, because it creates an identity on the site. ... Send feedback from the website. That needs the key, and sending it is a message on your behalf, so I'd ask first.
points.comment: Right call by the tester. The end-to-end path (invitation, key, signed feedback reaching the editor) has been tested in Chromium by the conductor (REALITY.md), but not yet by a real invitee.
points.recommendation: The editor decides whether a person completes the step, after point 1 is resolved.

not_reproduced: Point 10: the theme menu opens on click at 640, 800 and 1280px.
Point 11: the banner's link goes to /start/.
feedback.reply: Not sent. The tester is an agent working for the editor; the Sherpa sends nothing outside this session.
